summary: Lars Fogelin works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (ca. 1972–1997), Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn. He held a teaching post at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

Lati Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery. He served there as Abbot (ca. 1976–1984) and was a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia in ca. 1976.
Latika Lahiri was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958 and held a post at the University of Delhi from ca. 1969 to 1988.

Laura Harrington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, along with teachers Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, and Lobsang Jamspal, among others.

Lauran Hartley is a Tibetologist who served as a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University, an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University, a teacher at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and a consultant and editor at Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003).

Laurence Austine Waddell worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies after studying medicine at the University of Glasgow (ca. 1873–1878). He held posts in the British Army (ca. 1880–1908), Medical College Kolkata (1896), and University College London (1906–1908).

Laurie L. Patton specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard (ca. 1979–1983) and the University of Chicago (ca. 1983–1991), she held posts at Emory University (ca. 1996–2011), Duke University (ca. 2011–2015), and Middlebury College (ca. 2015).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as Professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Cornell University (ca. 1985–1989) and the University of Chicago (ca. 1990–1998) under Sheldon Pollock, later joining the faculty at Cornell University in ca. 2009.

Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012), having also studied at Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, College of Santa Fe, and St. John's College.

Le Manh That is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his BA at the University of Saigon (ca. 1961–1965), his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1965–1974), and held a post at Van Hanh University (ca. 1974–1975).

LeRoy Carr Barret was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Washington and Lee University (ca. 1894–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (ca. 1899–1903), where he studied under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Judith Zahler was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she studied under Jeffrey Hopkins from 1980 to 1981, and also studied with Harvey B. Aronson and Geshe Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. He served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University (attested 2011) and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

Leela Aditi Wood works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo M. Pruden was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taitetsu Unno (1960) and at the University of Tokyo (1964–1966) under Akira Hirakawa. He held posts at Brown University (1970–1971), Nyingma Institute (1971), and University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988).

Leo Meyer was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Theodor Benfey, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (ca. 1856–1865) and the Imperial University of Dorpat (ca. 1865–1898).

Leon Hurvitz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held professorial posts at the University of Washington (attested 1965–1973) and the University of British Columbia (ca. 1971–1988; attested 1990).

Leonard Bloomfield was a linguist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held academic posts at Cincinnati (ca. 1909–1910), Illinois (ca. 1910–1921), Ohio State (ca. 1921–1927), Chicago (ca. 1927–1940), and Yale (ca. 1940–1949).
